sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-FLAG M1 antibody labeling under non-permeabilized conditions (4°C). Receptor responds to agonist and undergoes internalization (L3), demonstrating preserved trafficking and signaling function.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly states the FLAG epitope was inserted after the signal peptide of full-length human PAR1, placing the tag at the mature N-terminus (after residue 21, before residue 22). Python confirms residue 21 = S (last of SP) and residue 22 = A (first of mature ectodomain). L3 and L4 independently confirm surface display by non-permeabilized anti-FLAG labeling, and L3 further demonstrates agonist-induced internalization, establishing functional competence. The N-terminal extracellular domain (22–102) is 81 residues from TM1, providing ample space for a short epitope tag. Full-length human PAR1 expressed in HEK293 cells with FLAG epitope inserted immediately after the signal peptide (residues 1–21) at the mature N-terminus (residue 22). Confirmed by non-permeabilized anti-FLAG M1 antibody labeling at 4°C in multiple cell lines (HeLa, Rat1 fibroblasts, HEK293). Receptor was also used for crystallography purification, confirming stable folded expression.

sources.claim: To facilitate purification, an N-terminal FLAG epitope was inserted after a signal peptide and a C-terminal deca-histidine tag was introduced.

literature_notes: L3 and L4 both corroborate the L1 site (FLAG after signal peptide, insert_after_residue=21) and elevate its validation to surface_and_function; they are not independent sites. L2 describes a T4 lysozyme insertion in the third intracellular loop (A301–A303, topology INTRACELLULAR 292–311) and is recorded in other_positions as intracellular. L5 describes SEAP reporter insertions at R41 and R46 — the canonical thrombin and APC cleavage sites in the extracellular N-terminal domain — but these constructs are explicitly designed to block protease-mediated receptor activation (R41Q and R46Q mutations abolish cleavage, and SEAP occludes the tethered-ligand region); they are recorded in other_positions as abrogates_function. No other ledger lines support additional surface tag sites.

literature_other_positions.note: T4 lysozyme (residues 2–161) inserted between A301 and A303 (removing V302) in the third intracellular loop (topology INTRACELLULAR 292–311); used for crystallography, not a surface tag site.
SEAP inserted at R41 (with R41Q mutation) to block thrombin cleavage and report APC cleavage; insertion at the canonical thrombin cleavage site abolishes normal tethered-ligand activation of PAR1.
SEAP inserted at R46 (with R46Q mutation) to block APC cleavage; insertion at this protease cleavage site disrupts normal receptor activation by APC.
